The first Studio Ghibli feature to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year was **“Princess Mononoke” (1997)**.  The film’s domestic box‑office run topped 1.5 billion yen, making it the highest‑grossing Japanese film at the time, and it was released internationally (including a U.S. theatrical run by Walt Disney Studios in 1999).  

That commercial triumph proved a turning point for Ghibli’s global profile.  It demonstrated that a Japanese animated feature could achieve both critical acclaim and mass‑market appeal abroad, encouraging major distributors to acquire Ghibli’s catalog and to invest in larger budgets for future projects.  The success of “Princess Mononoke” helped pave the way for later international breakthroughs—most notably “Spirited Away” winning the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature—and cemented Ghibli’s reputation as a world‑class animation studio.
